summary:
[  edit  ]
The Render Pick  DAT  lets you get information about the 3D surface at any pixel of any 3D render, allowing you to implement multi-touch on a 3D rendered scene. It samples a rendering (from a  Render TOP  or a  Render Pass TOP ) and returns 3D information from the geometry at the specified pick locations.
You feed it a  DAT  with minimum three columns:  select ,  u  and  v . A  Multi Touch In DAT  is usually connected to the Render Pick  DAT , where the Multi Touch In  DAT  points to a container that is displaying the output of the Render  TOP .
You can pick from multiple cameras simultaneously. You can specify a  camera  which allows the pick to occur from the point of a view other than the first camera listed in the  Render TOP . The value in the column can either be a path (relative to the Render Pick  DAT , or absolute) to a Camera  COMP , or it can be an integer index, started at 0. If it's an index it will select the camera to use if there are multiple cameras listed in the  Render TOP , or if there are cameras listed in the 'Custom Pick Camera(s)' parameter. This is useful for various  Multi-Camera Rendering  setups, and cases such as VR where your picking isn't coming from the point of view of your eye cameras, but instead hand controllers.
The pick location is a u,v (horizontal, vertical) coordinate placed in the table that you connect to the Render Pick  DAT  input.  Each row of the input table represents one pick point to be sampled, except for the first row which contains column headings  select ,  u  and  v  (plus any other unused columns you want).  The  select ,  u  and  v  columns are what you would get from a  Panel CHOP . The u and v values goes 0 to 1 left to right and bottom to top, no matter what the aspect ratio of the render is.
When Strategy is Always, that u,v location is always sampled and the results are displayed in the corresponding row in the Render Pick  DAT  output.
The output table will show the path of the geometry that was picked, its position (in a choice of reference frames), surface normal (excluding bump mapping), distance from camera, texture UV coordinate, color, alpha and instance id. It properly picks surfaces with deforming vertices.
There are some examples here:
geoPanel  in the palette.
multiTouch  in the palette under Techniques.
See also the single-sample  Render Pick CHOP .

parameters.label: Strategy
parameters.name: strategy
parameters.description: ⊞  - Decides when to update values based on pick interactions.

parameters.label: While Select
parameters.name: select
parameters.description: Continuously updates values when being selected/picked.

parameters.label: Hold First Picked
parameters.name: holdfirst
parameters.description: Holds the values first returned when geometry picked.

parameters.label: Hold Last Picked
parameters.name: holdlast
parameters.description: Holds the values last returned when geometry picked. This differs from the Continuous strategy in that it will hold the last values picked on geometry if the pick starts sampling empty space (no geometry in that part of the scene). Alternatively, using the Continuous strategy the values will be cleared to zero if the pick starts sampling empty space.

parameters.label: Always
parameters.name: always
parameters.description: Continuously updates values at the location picked.

parameters.label: Clear Previous Pick on New Pick
parameters.name: clearprev
parameters.description: This parameter is only enabled when the Strategy is set to Hold Last Picked. When this is on, starting a new pick on empty space will clear the values. When off, the last values will be held if the pick starts on empty space.

parameters.label: Response Time
parameters.name: responsetime
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines when the values are updated.

parameters.label: Next  Cook  (Faster)
parameters.name: nextcook
parameters.description: The values are captured on the current frame and updated next frame. Results are from the previous frame, but much faster cook times.

parameters.label: This  Cook  (Slower)
parameters.name: thiscook
parameters.description: The values are captured and updated in the current frame.

parameters.label: Pick Radius
parameters.name: pickradius
parameters.description: Controls the radius of the search area for the pick. If nothing is found at the pick's center it will keep searching for geometry in the search area defined by the Pick Radius.

parameters.label: Pick Radial Step
parameters.name: pickradstep
parameters.description: Used to reduce the searching within the search area. The search area is sampled at locations that correspond to 'spokes' outwards from the center pick point.

parameters.label: Pick Circular Step
parameters.name: pickcirstep
parameters.description: Used to reduce the searching within the search area. The search area is sampled at locations that correspond to 'rings' outwards from the center pick point.

parameters.label: Render/RenderPass  TOP
parameters.name: rendertop
parameters.description: Specifies which scene to pick on, and which camera to pick from. By default the first camera listed in the  Render TOP  will be used for picking. Another camera can be specified with the 'Custom Pick Camera(s)' parameter, and multiple different cameras can be selected using the  camera  input column.

parameters.label: Custom Pick Camera(s)
parameters.name: custompickcameras
parameters.description: Picking can be done from the viewport of custom camera(s) by specifying one or more  Camera COMP  here. If this parameter is blank the cameras from the Render  TOP  are used. To pick from the viewpoint of multiple different cameras, a  camera  column must be specified in the input  DAT .

parameters.label: Allow Multi-Camera  Rendering
parameters.name: allowmulticamera
parameters.description: Multi-Camera Rendering  is a faster way to render multiple passes at the same time, and is thus a speed improvement for doing many picks at the same time. This feature may not work correctly for some older  GLSL MATs  made in 088 though, so this parameter allows forcing off this speed improvement if necessary. Generally it should be left on though.

parameters.label: Use Pickable Flags
parameters.name: usepickableflags
parameters.description: When turned on only geometry whose  Pickable Flag  is on can be selected by the Render Pick  DAT . The Pickable  Flag  is found on all  Object  components.

parameters.label: Include Non-Pickable Objects
parameters.name: includenonpickable
parameters.description: Includes the non-pickable objects in the picking algorithm such that non-pickable objects may occlude pickable objects.  For example, if there is only one pickable object in the scene with lots of additional non-pickable geometry is present, turning this parameter on will prevent the pickable object from being selected if it is behind a non-pickage object (occluded by the non-pickage object).

parameters.label: Merge Input  DAT
parameters.name: mergeinputdat
parameters.description: Appends input table to the Render Pick DATs columns.

parameters.label: Activate Callbacks
parameters.name: activatecallbacks
parameters.description: Enables  Callback   DAT  for each pick event.

parameters.label: Callbacks  DAT
parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: Path  to a  DAT  containing callbacks for pick event received.

parameters.label: Reference   Object
parameters.name: referenceobj

parameters.label: Fetch Point Color
parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Returns the point color of the point picked on the geometry. Columns  cr, cg, cb, ca .

parameters.label: Fetch Texture UV
parameters.name: uv
parameters.description: Returns the texture coordinates of the point picked on the geometry. Columns  mapu, mapv, mapw .

parameters.label: Fetch Depth
parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Returns the depth of the point picked on the geometry. This value a non-linear ratio of the point's position between the near and far planes of the  Depth Buffer . Column is  depth .

parameters.label: Fetch  Instance  ID
parameters.name: instanceid
parameters.description: Returns the  Instance  ID of the object. This will always be 0 if instancing is off. Column is  instance .

parameters.label: To re-compute the output data of the  Operators . An operator cooks when (1) its inputs change, (2) its  Parameters  change, (3) when the timeline moves forward in some cases, or (4)  Scripting  commands are run on the node. When the operator is a  Panel Component , it also cooks when a user interacts with it. When an operator cooks, it usually causes operators connected to its output to re-cook.
